coverageBasis: Coverage is determined by the utility that owns the distribution wires, because that utility files the interconnection record. Retail generation providers do not change coverage: a community choice aggregator sells the electricity but does not own the wires, so its cities appear in full through the incumbent investor-owned utility. Only a publicly owned utility that owns its own distribution system creates a gap.

LADWP.name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power

independentBounds._comment: Keyed by the same normalised city key as wiresUtility. Each entry requires capacityMw, year, sourceName, sourceUrl, and scope. Candidate sources: EIA Form 861 Schedule 4 (net metering, utility-territory resolution) and CEC SB 379 / SolarAPP+ permit reporting (city resolution). Deliberately empty: no figure is published here until it comes from a citable source, and a territory-wide figure must declare scope 'service-territory' so it is never read as a city total.

notes.LOSANGELES: LADWP projects are outside the three-IOU source files; this total reflects only reported SCE/SDG&E/PG&E records and is a substantial lower bound.
notes.SACRAMENTO: SMUD projects are outside the three-IOU source files; this total is a substantial lower bound.
notes.SANTACLARA: Silicon Valley Power projects are outside the three-IOU source files; this total is a lower bound.
notes.PALOALTO: City of Palo Alto Utilities projects are outside the three-IOU source files; this total is a lower bound.

defaultPartialNote: This city has a publicly owned or municipal utility not represented in the PG&E, SCE, and SDG&E files; reported capacity is a lower bound.
defaultReportedNote: Projects were found in the PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E source files. Service-city grouping can still differ from legal boundaries.
defaultUnverifiedNote: No matching photovoltaic projects were found. This can mean zero reported capacity, a service-city mismatch, or utility coverage outside the source files.
